nodes.summary: Let $L \ge 1$, let $e$ be the exponent of $2$ in $L$ and let $f$ be the number of distinct odd prime factors of $L$. Then the number of integers $0 \le j < L$ with $\gcd(j, L) = 1$ and $j^2 \not\equiv 1 \pmod{L}$ is $\varphi(L) - 2^{f + g(e)}$, where $g(e) = \max(0, \min(2, e - 1))$.
nodes.title: Units modulo $L$ whose square is not $1$

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $L \ge 2$ be even. If the number of elements of multiplicative order $L$ in $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ equals $\varphi(L)$, then either $n = 4$ and $L = 2$, or $n = tq$ for some $t \in \{1, 2\}$ and some odd prime power $q$ with $L \mid \varphi(q)$.
nodes.title: Moduli with exactly $\varphi(L)$ units of even order $L$

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, the number of elements of multiplicative order $2$ in $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ is $2^k - 1$ for some natural number $k$.
nodes.title: Elements of order two modulo $n$

nodes.summary: Let $m$ and $j$ be natural numbers, $n \ge 1$ and $b \ge 2$. For a base $B$ write $d_j(B) = \lfloor m B^{j+1} / n \rfloor \bmod B$ for the $j$-th base-$B$ digit of $m/n$. Then there is a natural number $c < n$ such that $d_j(b + tn) = d_j(b) + tc$ for every natural number $t$.
nodes.title: Raising the base by multiples of $n$ shifts repetend digits linearly

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. If exactly two integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$ and $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ have multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$, then either $n = 3^k t \ge 9$ for some natural number $k$ and some $t \in \{1, 2\}$, or $n = p^k t$ for some prime $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, some $k \ge 1$ and some $t \in \{1, 2\}$.
nodes.title: Moduli with exactly two small bases of order six

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every $L > 2$, the number of integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$ and $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ whose multiplicative order modulo $n$ is $L$ is even.
nodes.title: Small bases of order greater than two come in pairs

nodes.title: Long division of a proper fraction

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $L$ be primes and let $b$ be a natural number of multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$. Suppose $m = 1$, or $2 \le m \le n - 1$ and $m$ has multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$. Then removing $1$ from the set of remainders $\{m b^j \bmod n : 0 \le j < L\}$ leaves exactly the set of integers $a$ with $2 \le a \le n - 1$ whose multiplicative order modulo $n$ is $L$.
nodes.title: Long-division remainders and small bases of prime order

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers and $u$ an integer, and put $b_2 = b^2 + un$. If $2 \le b_2 \le n - 2$, then $b \ne u + 1$.
nodes.title: A constraint on $b^2 + un$ between $2$ and $n - 2$

nodes.title: Half-period symmetry of the repetend of $1/n$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, let $i$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$ and $i \ge 2j$, put $n = p^i$ and $Q = p^j$, and let $b$ be a natural number whose multiplicative order modulo $n$ is $6Q$. nodes.title: Powers of $b^y \bmod p^i$ that differ by one

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $i$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$ and $i \ge 2j$, and let $b$ be a natural number whose multiplicative order modulo $p^i$ is $6p^j$. If $y$ and $s$ are natural numbers with $y \equiv s \pmod 6$, then $b^y \equiv b^s \pmod{p^j}$.
nodes.title: Powers of a base of order $6p^j$ modulo $p^j$ depend only on the exponent modulo $6$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, let $i$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$ and $i \ge 2j$, put $n = p^i$ and $Q = p^j$, and let $B < n$ be a natural number whose multiplicative order modulo $n$ is $6Q$. Let $z < 6Q$ be a natural number with $z \equiv 2 \pmod 6$ such that $zB \equiv 1 \pmod Q$ or $z \equiv 1 - B \pmod Q$. Then $B^z \bmod n = B - 1$.
nodes.title: A power of $B$ equal to $B - 1$ modulo $p^i$

Then $b_2 = b_1 - 1 + H$, $b_3 = n - 1$, $b_4 = n - b_1$ and…
nodes.title: Powers of a base of order $6$ modulo $tp^k$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, let $i$ and $j$ be natural numbers, put $n = p^i$ and $Q = p^j$, and let $B$ be a natural number whose multiplicative order modulo $n$ is $6Q$. Write $B_z = B^z \bmod n$. Then $B_{2Q} = B_Q - 1$, $B_{4Q} = B_{5Q} - 1$, $B_Q + B_{5Q} = n + 1$ and $B_{3Q} = n - 1$; moreover $Q^2 \equiv Q \pmod{6Q}$.

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $L \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and consider the repetend table of $1/n$ whose rows are the natural numbers $1 \le b < n$ coprime to $n$ of multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$, and whose column $j$ holds the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$. nodes.title: Columns $j$ and $j^{-1}$ of a repetend table match

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, let $k \ge 1$ and $t \in \{1, 2\}$, and put $n = t p^k$. Let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. Then column $4$ is different from column $0$ and from column $5$.
nodes.title: Column $4$ of the order-$6$ repetend table of $t p^k$ differs from columns $0$ and $5$

Let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. Then columns $0$ and $5$ are different.
nodes.title: Columns $0$ and $5$ of the order-$6$ repetend table of $t p^k$ differ

If there are exactly one or exactly three rows, then for all distinct $i, j < L$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.
nodes.title: Repetend tables with one or three rows have no matched columns

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $L$, let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $L$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. If there are at least one and at most three rows, then for all distinct $i, j < L$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.
nodes.title: Repetend tables with at most three rows have no matched columns

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $4$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. If there are exactly two rows, then for all distinct $i, j < 4$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.
nodes.title: Two-row repetend tables of length $4$ have no matched columns

If there are exactly two rows, then for all distinct $i, j < 3$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.
nodes.title: Two-row repetend tables of length $3$ have no matched columns

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ and $t \in \{1, 2\}$, and put $n = 3^k t$. Let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. Then for all distinct $i, j < 6$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.
nodes.title: Order-$6$ repetend tables of $3^k t$ have no matched columns

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime with $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$, let $k \ge 1$ and $t \in \{1, 2\}$, and put $n = t p^k$. Let the rows be the integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$, and let column $j$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{j+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over these rows. Then for all distinct $i, j \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ columns $i$ and $j$ are different.
nodes.title: Columns $1$ to $4$ of the order-$6$ repetend table of $t p^k$ are pairwise different

nodes.summary: Let $p \equiv 1 \pmod 6$ be prime, $k \ge 1$, $t \in \{1, 2\}$ and $n = t p^k$, and let $B$ be the set of integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$, $\gcd(b, n) = 1$ and multiplicative order $6$ modulo $n$. For $c \ge 0$ let column $c$ be the multiset of the digits $\lfloor b^{c+1}/n \rfloor \bmod b$ over $b \in B$. Then for every $i \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $j \in \{0, 5\}$, columns $i$ and $j$ are different multisets.
nodes.title: Columns $1$, $2$, $3$ of the order-$6$ repetend table differ from columns $0$ and $5$

nodes.title: Differences of repetend digits

Then $b$ and $b'$ have the same digit in column $L - 1$: $\lfloor b'^{L}/n \rfloor \bmod b' = \lfloor b^{L}/n \rfloor \bmod b$.

nodes.title: The number of units of order $L$ is a multiple of $\varphi(L)$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
